title: Reading Drill — Choosing library study chairs — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Choosing library study chairs — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The library facilities team had been asked to investigate chairs being moved into aisles during busy sessions in Cairnford. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on the width of clear paths, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a ten-week comparison, the team used floor measurements at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because changes in occupancy might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward chairs with smaller footprints. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
